newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends higher in quiet, rangebound trade.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends higher in quiet, rangebound trade.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended a choppy session higher but remained rangebound in seasonally quiet trade, pit sources said.

"The market opened lower under some pressure from hedging," one floor source said. "Once we got through that and were trading back around unchanged, the bids came back up. We're just stuck in a trading range."
Traders said selling interest dried up around $11.23 per cwt in the July, near the $11.21 level where the May contract expired on Tuesday. Buyers were hard to find above the $11.40 level, they said.
Louis Dreyfus was said to be a light buyer on the day while LIT was a net seller.
Rice ended three cents per cwt higher across the board with July at $11.40. Volume was estimated by CBOT at 300 lots, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 221 lots.
